Reports also show crashes tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 1 and 3 p.m., a pattern worth knowing if you're piecing together what happened. We are not a law firm, and we don't represent you directly — we simply make the introduction. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. If you were hurt in a crash on one of these local corridors, or anywhere else in town, reaching out costs nothing and may help you understand your options.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act early.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the accident, you may still recover damages — reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated by it.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That means the initial consultation and case review cost you nothing.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Hillsborough?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your injury involved a government vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's wise to speak with an attorney promptly to avoid missing a filing window.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be shared in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Hillsborough?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes along corridors like I-280, the I-280 northbound stretch, Skyline Boulevard, and Crystal Springs Road, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 1 and 3 p.m. These are simply counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service that helps injured people find an independent personal injury attorney. We don't provide legal representation ourselves — we make the introduction, and the attorney you're connected with handles your case.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you recover compensation. The initial conversation and case evaluation are free, with no obligation to move forward.
